subject: Kestrel renewal: deferred pricing and burst top-up request
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@kestrel.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@kestrel.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal negotiation — request to defer portion of committed spend

Hi Stephanie,

Hope you’re well. Kestrel’s renewal comes up in December and we’re trying to strike a path that keeps the low-latency SLA in place but eases cash flow for Q1. We ran the Q3 usage export (attached) and expect a 25% uplift in production inference over the next 12 months if we ship a new feature. That said, our CFO has asked for a short-term cash relief mechanism.

Two requests for your team to consider: 
- Defer invoicing on 20% of the committed capacity until end of Q2 2027 (we would still be contractually committed to the capacity, but invoice timing shifts)
- Provide a 6-month price-hold on the committed rate for the increase we’re agreeing to today (we can discuss phasing).

We’d be comfortable increasing the committed baseline by +30% if you can accommodate the above, plus a small burst-topup credit to cover an expected spike during our product launch window.

Can you confirm if Redwood can structure deferment + conditional price-hold? If yes, we’ll loop in procurement and legal to speed the SOW/Amendment.

Best,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Platform Partnerships
Kestrel.ai

[Attachment: Kestrel_usage_Q3.csv (csv)]

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@kestrel.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation — request to defer portion of committed spend

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the usage file. Appreciate the context (congrats on the launch runway). We can get creative here; high level thoughts: 

1) Deferred invoicing: we can offer a deferred invoicing schedule for up to 20% of the committed ARR for 6 months. That would mean Redwood recognizes the commitment (and capacity is reserved) but invoices are pushed out; we’d treat the deferred portion as a short-term receivable and can add a small amortization fee if needed (finance to confirm).

2) Conditional price-hold: we can lock the committed per-token rate for 6 months for the incremental uplift (+30% baseline) if Kestrel keeps a minimum utilization floor (we propose 60% of the new baseline). If utilization falls below the floor, we would step the per-token rate to a predefined fallback tier.

3) Burst top-up credit: we can provide a one-time burst credit equal to 50k tokens (applies to bursts only, auto-expire in 90 days post-launch).

Next steps: would you like a single amendment (defer + price-hold + burst credit) or separate exhibits? If you want, I’ll draft the commercial terms and share a redlineable SOW for procurement/legal. I’ve cc’d Ben (sales lead) and Vivek (revenue ops) to validate the economics and Monica for post-sale support.

If this sounds viable I can send a draft by EOD tomorrow.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mobile: (415) 555-0192

Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick turn — the framework you outlined is workable. Procurement prefers a single amendment for speed. A couple of clarifications before we route to legal: 

- For the deferred invoicing: Kestrel is ok with a 2% one-time amortization fee on the deferred amount.
- For the utilization floor: we’d ask for a 30-day cure period before any fallback rate applies. That should give us time to correct rollout issues.
- Burst credit: acceptable; can it be converted to additional capacity at a pro-rated rate if unused? If not, no problem — we’ll plan consumption.

If you can provide a redlineable amendment with these bullets, our procurement team will prioritize review and we’ll aim to sign within 5 business days. I’ve attached an updated usage snapshot.

Elena
